identity.gender_note: Recorded as a masculine given name (Wiktionary marks حَمْزَة as a male given name); it is not used as a girl's name in mainstream naming practice.

core_meaning.short_meaning: Strong, steadfast; an Arabic epithet for the lion
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Hamza (Arabic حَمْزَة, Ḥamza) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning “strong and steadfast”; it is also recorded as an Arabic epithet for the lion. Its prominence in Muslim naming comes from Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal uncle of the Prophet Muhammad, who was renowned for his strength and courage.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Lion (a rare, obsolete Arabic noun sense of حَمْزَة)
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Dictionaries of Muslim names gloss Hamza as “strong, steadfast” and note that it serves as an epithet for the lion; Wiktionary records an obsolete Arabic noun حَمْزَة meaning “lion”. The lion association is reinforced by the title of the Prophet’s uncle Hamza, remembered as Asad Allah (“Lion of God”). The everyday sense parents intend is strength and steadfast courage.

etymology.morphology: Feminine-pattern noun form (ending in tāʾ marbūṭa, ـة) on the root ح م ز, used as a masculine name — a common pattern in Arabic names (compare Usama, Muʿawiya).
etymology.etymology_explanation: Hamza is the Arabic word حَمْزَة used directly as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form. Wiktionary lists it under the root ح م ز with a rare, obsolete noun sense “lion”.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: Do not confuse ḥamza (حمزة, with ḥāʾ ح) with hamza (همزة, with hāʾ ه), the Arabic glottal-stop sign ء. They are spelled with different letters and are unrelated.

language_notes.primary: Arabic is the language of the recorded form حمزة.
language_notes.usage: Other scripts are transliterations of the name into those writing systems; they are not independent origins.

origin.origin_explanation: Arabic in origin; spread with Islam across the Arab world and into Turkish, Persian, Urdu, Malay and Caucasian naming, largely in honour of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

religion.primary_association: Islamic — name of a Companion and uncle of the Prophet
religion.religious_status: Honoured Islamic name through a Companion of the Prophet; not a Qur'anic word
religion.religious_explanation: Hamza is not mentioned in the Qur'an, but it is one of the most respected names in Islamic history because it was borne by Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (c. 568–625), the Prophet’s paternal uncle and milk-brother, an early convert (616 CE), a commander at Badr, and a martyr of the Battle of Uhud, honoured as Sayyid al-Shuhadāʾ (“Leader of the Martyrs”).

quranic_status.note: The name Hamza does not occur in the Qur'an; its Islamic standing comes from the Companion Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

hadith_status.note: No specific authentic hadith report about this name is cited; none is invented.

prophetic_status.note: No verified source establishes Hamza as the name of a prophet.

companion_status.reference: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (c. 568–625 CE) — paternal uncle and milk-brother of the Prophet Muhammad; embraced Islam in 616 CE; killed at the Battle of Uhud on 23 March 625 CE; titled Sayyid al-Shuhadāʾ and Asad Allah wa Asad Rasūlih (“Lion of God and of His Messenger”).
companion_status.note: Hamza is the name of the Prophet’s uncle and Companion, Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

islamic_naming_context.context: Used throughout the Muslim world — Arab countries, Turkey, Iran, South and Southeast Asia, Africa and the Caucasus — usually in honour of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Parents choose it for its sense of strength and steadfastness and for its association with a celebrated Companion.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Its religious esteem comes from the Companion who bore it, not from Qur'anic usage.

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: Across Muslim cultures the name evokes bravery and loyalty, after the Companion’s defence of the Prophet.
cultural_context.personal_name_interpretation: As a personal name it can be read as a wish for the quality it names.
cultural_context.interpretation_warning: The symbolic reading is a cultural convention, distinct from the dictionary sense.
cultural_context.impact: The legendary adventures of Amir Hamza are told in the Hamzanama (Dastan-e-Amir Hamza), a Persian romance that became a major Urdu storytelling tradition and was famously illustrated for the Mughal emperor Akbar.

spiritual_meaning.meaning: Families often choose Hamza hoping the child will share the steadfast courage and loyalty associated with the Prophet’s uncle.
spiritual_meaning.basis: Lexical meaning (strong, steadfast) and the example of Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.

personality_associations.note: No verified basis links this name to specific personality traits.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hamza total 4, associated with stability, discipline and order. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.
numerology.note: Numerology is an optional interpretive layer.

faq.a: Hamza is an Arabic name meaning “strong, steadfast”; it is also an Arabic epithet for the lion.
Yes. It is one of the most honoured names in Islam because it was borne by Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet Muhammad’s uncle and Companion.
Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib (c. 568–625) was the Prophet’s paternal uncle and milk-brother. He embraced Islam in 616 CE, fought at Badr and was martyred at Uhud in 625 CE.

faq.q: Why is Hamza called the Lion of God?
faq.a: Early sources give him the title Asad Allah wa Asad Rasūlih — “Lion of God and of His Messenger” — for his bravery; he is also called Sayyid al-Shuhadāʾ, “Leader of the Martyrs”.

faq.q: Is Hamza mentioned in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. The name does not occur in the Qur'an; its religious standing comes from the Companion who bore it.

faq.q: What is the origin of Hamza?
faq.a: Hamza is Arabic (حَمْزَة), from the root ح م ز, and spread through the Muslim world with Islam.

faq.q: What does Hamza mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu it is written حمزہ and means “طاقتور، ثابت قدم” (strong, steadfast); it is also a title of the lion (شیر).
HAM-zuh. In Arabic the first sound is the breathy ḥ (/ˈħamza/); Urdu speakers say /ˈhəmzə/.

faq.q: Is Hamza a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Hamza is a masculine name used for boys.

faq.q: What are other spellings of Hamza?
faq.a: Hamzah, Humza, Hamzeh, Hamsah and Khamzat are spellings of the same name in different languages.

faq.q: Is Hamza the same as the Arabic letter hamza?
faq.a: No. The name is spelled with ḥāʾ (حمزة), while the glottal-stop sign hamza (همزة, ء) is spelled with hāʾ; they are different words.
